How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF DECEMBER 2, 2024
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Duong called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at 6:30
P.M. on Monday, December 2, 2024, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at
City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Rodriguez.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nancy Duong, Justin Lotz, Darwin Rodriguez, Ting Xie

Commissioners Absent:  Davis Barrantes

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  DECEMBER 2, 2024
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The Commission had an edit to the minutes and a motion was made by Commissioner
  Rodriguez, seconded by Commissioner Lotz, to approve the amended minutes of the
  Community Services Commission Meeting for November 4, 2024.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 3-0-1-1 as follows:

  AYES:  DUONG, LOTZ, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  XIE
  ABSENT:  BARRANTES

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. YOUTH AMBASSADOR APPLICATION REVIEW
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  The Commission would like to approve the late applicants and provide priority to the
  ones that were received on time. They discussed the special meeting for interviews and
  the time limit per candidate. Interviews will be held on Thursday, December 12th.

  Public Comment: None

  B. EVENTS AND PROGRAMS UPDATES
  Presented by Supervisors Shoup & Casillas, and Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  The Commission inquired about event turnout compared to previous ones and
  expressed interest in meeting the new Public Information Officer about the social
  media strategy for future events.

  A commissioner praised the event's organization and raised questions about
  registration, food truck visibility, and the queue at the haunted zone. They suggested
  considering a fast pass fee for attractions and making food truck pricing more
  prominent.

  Another commissioner proposed requesting donations instead of charging for
  attractions. Feedback for the Turkey Trot included using more signage and cones next
  year.

  The Commission suggested informing families about the need to set up new accounts
  in the updated system and inquired about merging past activity history with new
  accounts. They also asked if RideSG+ users would receive priority after the changes
  and how these would be communicated.
COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  DECEMBER 2, 2024
   Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Duong.

  The Commissioners would like to focus on ways to collect data from people who attend
  events and programs. Commissioners asked for an update regarding translation
  services and if the volunteer received a certificate or letter. The Commission would like
  to assist with recruiting student volunteers for future events and programs.

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS
  Commissioner Xie thanked the commission and Chair Duong for leading the meetings in her
  absence.

  Commissioner Lotz liked that wood chips were added at the playground. He appreciated the
  added safety to the parks.

  Commissioner Rodriguez- appreciates working with the team.

  Chair Duong thanked staff for all their efforts and looks forward to attending the Holiday Tree
  Lighting.

6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Matthew shared info regarding the upcoming mission playhouse programs.

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Duong adjourned the meeting at 7:53 p.m.

  The next regular meeting held on Monday, January 6, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City
  Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  January 6, 2025

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Ana Casillas, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Youth Sports Programming 2024 Recap

San Gabriel Youth Sports Program
The City of San Gabriel Community Services Department offered a full year of
programming at Jefferson Middle School for grades 6-8, during 2024. Each sport season
offered participants a chance to learn sports fundaments, build skills, provide game play,
provide homework help, and enrichment activities. Each sport season held practices
Monday- Friday from the bell until 5pm.

From November to March, basketball was offered with a varsity boys and a varsity girls
team for a total of 30 participants. These teams competed in the 210 league and some
friendly games with teams in the Southern California Municipal Athletic Federation
(SCMAF). After competing with both leagues, it was determined the SCMAF league was
the best fit for our teams both in skill level and sportsmanship.

Soccer was also offered February 5 through March 29 with a boys varsity team and a girls
varsity team for a total of 32 participants. These teams competed in the 210 league and
while players learned a lot the 210 league proved to be on a much more competitive level
than our teams.

The Jefferson Sports Academy was offered during the summer months, from June 12
through July 10, and focused on three sports Volleyball, Basketball and Soccer. This clinic
offered a chance to learn the fundamentals of each sport, enhance passion for athletics,
and highlight sportsmanship. This summer had a total of 59 participants.

For the Fall, Volleyball and Flag Football were offered with a total 71 kids participating.
Each sport offered two varsity teams and one JV team with practices held Monday- Friday
running September 3 through December 20 from the bell until 5pm. Both sports
 competed in the San Gabirel Valley SCMAF league with Flag Football garnering second
place in the SCMAF Tournament in November.

Staff is looking forward to continuing to build and enhance the sports program. Basketball
season will be starting January 6 and Soccer season will be held in the spring.
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  January 6, 2025

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Andy Shoup, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Department Special Event Report- 2024

Holiday Tree Lighting

The 48th annual Holiday Tree Lighting was held in Plaza Park on Tuesday, December 3,
from 6:00pm-8:30pm, with an estimated 2,000 community members in attendance. The
night began with the return of the Taste of San Gabriel event, trackless train rides, craft
booths, and performances by the Dewey Woodcraft Rangers, Department Dance Groups,
Roosevelt Music Immersion Experience, and the San Gabriel Marching Band. At 7pm the
Mayor and City Council, with assistance from the Roosevelt choir, led the community in a
countdown to light the tree, followed by the arrival of Santa Claus, who was escorted by
the San Gabriel Police and Fire Departments.

Following its success at the Fall Fun Festival, a pre-registration option was offered for the
trackless train and photos with Santa sections; this allowed families to explore the event
without spending an excessive amount of time in line. Additionally, this year we also
added two other photo locations, one of which included a photobooth.

Looking toward the 2025 event, scheduled for December 2nd, staff will be exploring ways
to continue the event success, as well as expand with more interactive opportunities,
holiday themed amenities, and of course, more lights!
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  December 2, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2024 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting. The draft for 2024 outlined in this report
includes items from the 2023 workplan and the amendments made at the November 6,
2023 and February 5, 2024 commission meetings. The Community Services Commission
approved the workplan at the March 4, 2024 commission meeting. At the October 7, 2024
commission meeting the Community Services Commission decided to change it from an
annual workplan to an ongoing document that can be adjusted if and when needed to
better address the needs of the department. The Commission will conduct a
comprehensive evaluation of the workplan every six months to determine if major
changes need to be made.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.
 Purpose of the Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.

Current Workplan
The workplan sets four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore. The list below reflects amendments made at the November 4,
2024 Community Services Commission Meeting.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Provide new programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.

Next Steps:
  1. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  a. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
  2. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  a. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information.

Completed Tasks:
  1. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to assist
  in the development and implementation of events and services.
  a. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native American
  Community and interfaith groups
  2. Recommend that City Council approve the release of an RFP for a new
  registration software during fiscal year 2024/25.
 3. Recommend that City Council approve the addition of a part time case manager
  through a third party provider.
4. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
5. Commission to develop a youth ambassador program, host interviews and appoint
  two non-voting ambassadors to the commission.
